title: Don’t Go Backward on China Policy
gist: Wyne and Hass argue Trump's transactional, Xi-centric China policy has cut U.S. leverage and pushed allies to hedge, but warn that a hawkish restoration by Democrats and moderate Republicans after the 2026 midterms would be a mistake. They cite failing export controls, China's lead in EVs, robots and life sciences, and polling showing Americans, especially the young, favor cooperation, and urge 'steady competence': managed coexistence, AI guardrails with Beijing, reindustrialization, and narrowing tariffs.
